issues.description: The solution repository adds an 'age' attribute to Animal and implements constructors that require (String name, int age) for Animal and all subclasses, whereas the problem statement UML and the template code (Main.java) show/expect animals to be constructed with only a name. This mismatch between the solution and the problem/template will confuse students about the required constructor signatures and the class attributes they must initialize.
issues.suggestedFix: Either remove the additional 'age' attribute and the two-argument constructors from the solution (make Animal and subclasses use a single-argument constructor that only initializes 'name') to match the UML and template Main examples, or update the problem statement, UML, and template (including Main.java examples and task descriptions) to explicitly include the 'age' attribute and require two-argument constructors (String name, int age). Ensure all three artifacts consistently specify the same attributes and constructor signatures.

issues.description: Constructor/attribute mismatch for Animal and its subclasses: the problem statement and the template Main() examples imply Animal (and Seal/Pig/Goat) should be constructed with a single 'name' parameter, but the solution introduces an additional 'age' attribute and two-argument constructors (String name, int age). This inconsistency changes the conceptual shape of the Animal entity (constructor signature and attributes) across artifacts and is likely to confuse students when mapping the requirements to the implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Animal abstraction consistent across artifacts: either (A) remove the extra 'age' attribute from the solution and change the Animal and subclass constructors to accept only (String name) to match the problem description and template Main examples, or (B) update the problem statement and template examples to declare and demonstrate the additional 'age' attribute and two-argument constructors (String name, int age). Choose one approach and apply it uniformly to Animal.java, Seal.java, Pig.java, Goat.java, the UML/problem text, and the template Main() usage.
